title: The Stray Dog Who Became A Sergeant
description:
Sergeant Stubby (1915-1926) was a dog who became the unofficial mascot of the 102nd Infantry Regiment and served with the 26th (Yankee) Division in World War I. He was found wandering the Yale campus in July 1917 while soldiers trained, and Corporal Robert Conroy hid him on the ship to France. He served 18 months, took part in 17 battles and four offensives, saved his regiment from surprise mustard gas attacks and found and comforted the wounded. He has been called the most decorated war dog of the Great War and the only dog nominated and promoted to sergeant through combat. His preserved body is on display at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.

Source: Wikipedia, 'Sergeant Stubby'.
